decisions.title: C# with Unity as the host
decisions.note: Core is an engine-free netstandard2.1 library (C# 9) so it builds and tests in CI without Unity; Unity references it as a local package.

decisions.title: Step 1 = isolated modules, no game loop
decisions.note: Each of the 17 researched systems becomes a module with its own tests before any loop or renderer.

decisions.title: Every citizen is a full agent
decisions.note: RimWorld-depth needs/mood/health/skills/jobs per person at civilization scale. Population target: as large as we can; the performance ceiling is a later bridge.

decisions.title: Large authored tech tree of societal evolution
decisions.note: Endless/procedural tech comes later; the research module's data model must not preclude it.

decisions.title: Director persona name
decisions.note: RimWorld's storyteller is translated into a chronicle-style narrator targeting YOUR civilization. Working candidates: Scribe, Historian, The Chronicle. Code module stays 'Director' until chosen.

decisions.title: Launch only when it makes sense
decisions.note: Tracker shows launch disabled with the reason until a playable loop exists.

decisions.title: Living tracker
decisions.note: Third tab in the Blueprint, generated from docs/status.json; repo-verified items are locked, remaining items are tick-able and persisted for everyone who opens the page.

decisions.title: Duplicate defName policy: later pack wins
decisions.note: Implementation choice mirroring mod load-order semantics (DefLoadOptions.DuplicatePolicy is switchable). Revisit when mod patching lands.

decisions.title: Auto-merge green PRs
decisions.note: PRs are merged as soon as CI is green; no manual merge step.

decisions.title: RimWorld's static Rand and Scribe stay static, but per thread
decisions.note: Ported call sites (Rand.Value, Scribe_Values.Look) keep their shape; state is [ThreadStatic] so tests and worker threads never share a sequence or a save session. Explicit RandomStream instances are the preferred form for new systems.

decisions.title: Two clocks; time never causes progression
decisions.note: The ported 60-tick clock stays authoritative. An abstracted clock above it exists only to skip, and may only do what the real clock would have done — every process it advances needs a sampled equivalent that agrees with ticking. A century of abstract time with no people, food or research advances nothing. Spec section 11.1.

decisions.title: Civilization-wide sight, settlement-deep touch
decisions.note: Attention follows RimWorld's world-map/colony-map split, which World/ and Map/ already mirror. Global sight and indirect verbs at civilization scope; any citizen openable at settlement scope. The missing seam is the settlement interior. Spec section 11.2.

decisions.title: Citizens tier by significance, and the tier is the historical record
decisions.note: Full / Interval / Statistical, promoted by attention, role, chronicle mention or relation — never by distance or elapsed time; identity survives demotion. Fidelity is written at the tier lived and never upgraded, so the deep past is thin because it was thin. One mechanism pays for both performance and the fiction. Spec section 11.3-11.4.

decisions.title: A game opens region first, then site, Manor Lords style
decisions.note: The world map is browsed by region; inside the chosen region, markers show water, soil, timber, stone, clay, flint, ore, salt, game, fords and high ground, and the player places the settlement centre. Deposits are derived from existing terrain rather than sprinkled. Founding band is 20-40 people in several households. Spec section 5b.

decisions.title: One civilization at world generation; rivals emerge later
decisions.note: World gen places the player's faction alone. Other civilizations emerge from the simulation over time rather than existing at time zero. The cost — factions, trade and diplomacy idle through the opening — is accepted for the truer sticks-and-stones arc. Spec section 5b.4.

decisions.title: No fixed horizon — the director paces time
decisions.note: Decided: years are not the currency, attention-worthy moments are. A civilization runs on the abstracted clock by default and drops into ticked time when the storyteller judges a moment worth watching — RimWorld's own TimeSlower inverted, and TimeSlower is already ported. A century in which nothing happened costs nothing to pass, which is what makes the endless sticks-to-exotic arc playable at all: at the real clock, 200 ticked years would be 222 hours at maximum speed. The tech tree is therefore priced against moments per era rather than years, and the 'dry at day 3,074' measurement is a function of a unit that no longer applies. Spec section 11.1.

decisions.title: The population ceiling is health-tracker cost
decisions.note: Measured: 14 milliseconds per pawn-day at N<=500 (an earlier note said microseconds, off by a thousand), 15x speed holds to roughly 2,500-5,000 healthy pawns, and HealthTick is 75.4% of all per-pawn tick cost. Two fixes landed: making the hot capacity path non-allocating cut garbage 31x (4,232 MB to 138 MB per 1,000 pawn-days, 33 Gen0 collections to 1), and caching the per-tick death check behind the existing dirty flag took a further 7-12% (measured A/B, same box same minute). The remaining cost is spread rather than concentrated, so the next real lever for population scale is the citizen tiering in spec section 11.3, not another micro-optimization. Sick pawns remain far worse: 3 untended injuries measured 24.8x. See docs/perf/baseline.md.

decisions.title: Citizen tiering is built next, before the god layer
decisions.note: It is the most invasive change remaining — it touches every tracker and every system that assumes a pawn is fully simulated — so the god layer should be written against tiered citizens rather than retrofitted to them. RimWorld already proves the Statistical tier works: its world pawns keep identity, relationships and ageing while needs, jobs and health stop ticking, and AgeTickMothballed is already ported. The tiers and the abstracted clock are one mechanism: dropping into ticked time is promoting the attended settlement to Full. Spec section 11.3.

decisions.title: Coal is its own deposit, and tradeable
decisions.note: Coal decided where industry went, so it gets its own category rather than hiding inside Ore: a site chosen in the neolithic for water and game may or may not turn out to be an industrial one, and the player will not know for centuries. Geography shapes rather than dictates — caravans can supply a settlement that lacks coal, at a cost, which is what actually happened and gives the ported trade system real work in the industrial era. Spec section 5b.

systems.translation: Implemented: planet generation at civilization scale — biomes, rivers and roads unchanged; the player's civilization alone at world gen, many rival civilizations seeded over time instead by World.EmergenceManager, population-scaled and era-seeded off the world's current era.

items.label: Icosphere tile grid (10·4ⁿ+2 tiles, 5/6 neighbours, lat/long) with coverage → subdivision
Seeded Perlin/ridged-multifractal noise → elevation (~32% land), hilliness, temperature by latitude and elevation, rainfall, swampiness
14 biome workers scoring tiles (ocean/lake by water-body size; tundra…rainforest; deserts)
Rivers flow downhill by flow thresholds; roads path between settlements over hilliness/biome cost
Minimal FactionDef/Faction + settlement placement (counts, min distance, biome weight); world save regenerates the grid from its seed
Faction relations and tech levels seeded at world generation

Translation: many rival civilizations at planet scale — population scaling and era seeding — World.EmergenceManager, MTB-paced off OverallPopulation and gated by Research.ResearchManager.CurrentEra so nothing emerges more advanced than the world's own most advanced known civilization

systems.translation: Settlement-site maps, many per civilization, generated on demand from the world tile via MapGen.MapGenerator.GenerateMapFor, rather than RimWorld's single fixed map. Rocky outcrops, ore veins and river channels are not sprinkled independently of the world map: their presence and rough scale are read directly from the tile's own Ore/Stone/river data, so a tile the world map promised ore or a river on always produces a map with ore or a river crossing it. Ruins (GenStep_Ruins) are a direct, hand-written stand-in for RimWorld's RuleDef/SymbolResolver ruin grammar rather than a port of that grammar itself: one ruin shape (a gap-and-rubble wall rectangle, sometimes roofed, sometimes looted, walls weathered off full hit points), not a composable rule library. GenStep_ScatterShrines (a single guarded unique-reward structure) and corpses inside a ruin are not ported at all — no Corpse Thing/system exists yet in this port, and a flavor-only stand-in was judged to misrepresent rather than simplify a dead pawn's identity; see GenStep_Ruins's own doc comment.

items.label: Terrain layer from tile biome, fertility/rainfall noise and swampiness (soil, rich soil, sand, gravel, marsh), plus a carved river channel where the tile carries one

Elevation/fertility noise → rocky outcrops and mountains as natural edifices, scaled by tile hilliness and the Stone deposit magnitude (per-map quantile calibration, mirroring WorldGenStep_Terrain's land-fraction technique)

Cave systems (directional random walk, not cellular automata) carved through mountain, with mineable ore veins guaranteed proportional to the tile's Ore deposit magnitude and a yield table (mineableThing/mineableYield)
Roofs (thick/thin) over solid mountain and enclosed cave passages via the RoofGrid, graded by local rock density rather than a border flood fill (a mined tunnel stays roofed along its length)
Scatterers: loose rock chunks and wild plant growth, densities read from the tile's Stone/Timber deposit magnitudes and biome plant density
MapGenerator.GenerateMapFor(worldTile): a settlement's interior generated from the world tile it sits on — the §11.2 seam between the World and Map layers

GenStep_Ruins: weathered wall rectangles with gaps and rubble scattered onto the map, some roofed, some carrying loot, material and roofing drawn from content; deterministic per seed, density scaling with map area, and structurally guaranteed (plus region-graph tested) never to wall a pawn into an unreachable pocket. GenStep_ScatterShrines and ruin corpses are not ported — see the module's own doc comment

World-tile roads (RoadDef/tile.Roads) carried onto the local map as a street of the road's own local terrain (RoadDef.localTerrain), entering and leaving on the sides that face the neighbouring tiles the road actually connects — direction read from WorldGrid tile positions via GenStep_Roads

Entering a settlement at settlement scope triggers GenerateMapFor and persists the result on the WorldObject — Settlement.EnterMap, generated once on first entry, sized by TotalPopulation, cached and Scribe round-tripped

systems.translation: Unchanged. The Thing/Comp runtime and map grids every later system stands on; settlement maps are generated onto it.

items.label: Geometry: IntVec3/IntVec2, Rot4, CellRect, GenAdj, GenRadial, CellIndices

Pawn is a Thing: identity, map presence, hit points and ticking move onto ThingWithComps
Terrain, roof, thing, edifice and path grids with path-cost recalculation
ListerThings and MapPawns: per-def, per-group and per-map bookkeeping
