Region / RegionLink graph over the map's passability (Region, RegionLink, RegionGrid, RegionMaker, RegionAndRoomUpdater), cardinal flood fill with doors as their own Portal regions, torn down and re-flooded only for the region(s) a passability change actually touches — AI's Reachability is the consumer

systems.translation: Proposed: citizen generation. Birth and lineage drive most generation instead of 'wanderer joins'; backstories become life histories written by the sim.

items.label: Backstory pairs (childhood/adulthood): skill gains, disabled work tags, forced traits
Trait rolls by commonality with degrees, conflicts and required work tags
Skill levels from age-scaled curves plus backstory and trait gains; passion rolls
NameTriple/NameSingle from gendered name banks, unique across a population
Life stages and age tracker: biological/chronological ticks, body size, health scale and hunger factors per stage
Appearance: melanin and body type only — hair and palette land with the renderer
Translation: newborn generation and life events — birth and lineage as the main source of citizens is still open

Weapon half: PawnKindDef.weaponTags/weaponMoneyRange + PawnWeaponGenerator, matched against ThingDef.weaponTags/techLevel/MarketValue and capped at the generated pawn's own Faction.def.techLevel; wired into PawnGenerator's pipeline and carried on the new Pawn_EquipmentTracker (Pawn.equipment), Scribe round-trip included. Apparel half now built too — see pawngen.apparel.

Apparel half of gear: ThingDef.apparel/ApparelProperties (body part groups, ApparelLayerDef, tags) plus Pawn_ApparelTracker — wearing an item registers it as a real Combat.IArmorSource through the pre-existing PawnArmor hook, no Combat code touched. PawnApparelGenerator consumes PawnKindDef.apparelTags/apparelMoneyRange the way PawnWeaponGenerator consumes weaponTags, wired into PawnGenerator after the lifespan roll so it never perturbs an RNG-sensitive step any other test already pins. Six ThingDefs ship (Apparel_Basic.xml) with real ArmorRating_*/Insulation stats and CompQuality. Tests: tests/SimWorld.Core.Tests/Things/ApparelTests.cs (filed with CompQuality/apparel content rather than under Pawns, per this pass's test-directory ownership).

Genes / xenotypes with inheritance (Biotech): GeneDef (statOffsets/statFactors/capMods/disabledWorkTags/biostatCpx/biostatMet/lifespanBonusYears/exclusionTags) + XenotypeDef (a named germline), Pawn_GeneTracker (endogenes/xenogenes, exclusionTags conflict resolution) reusing StatWorker/PawnCapacityUtility/CombinedDisabledWorkTags/HungerRate rather than a parallel pipeline; PawnGenerationRequest.Xenotype applied by PawnGenerator strictly downstream of every existing roll (zero RNG cost when unset); FamilyManager birth-path inheritance (GeneInheritanceUtility) — shared endogenes breed true, a single-parent endogene is a 50% coin flip, xenogenes never inherit. RimWorld's exact inheritance-selection and metabolism-to-hunger curves were not sourced in this sandbox — see GeneTuning's own doc; pinned by property tests instead of literals. Content: 14 GeneDefs, 4 XenotypeDefs (Baseliner + 3 non-baseline).

systems.translation: Unchanged. Tick engine, rare/long tick buckets, deterministic RNG streams, Scribe-style save/load. Bucket sizing scales with population.

items.label: TickManager: 60 ticks/s clock, TimeSpeed multipliers (1/3/6/15), pause/toggle, danger-forced normal speed
TickList buckets: normal / rare (250) / long (2000) with deferred register/deregister
Tick order: pre-tickers (world, map) → normal → rare → long → post-tickers; per-frame tick cap drops backlog
MurmurHash-based RandomStream per system + thread-safe static Rand facade (Range/Chance/Gaussian/MTB/PushState)
GenTicks / GenDate: 60,000-tick days, quadrums, years, longitude-local time, seasons by latitude
Scribe: IExposable save/load in three passes (LoadingVars → ResolvingCrossRefs → PostLoadInit)
Scribe_Values / Defs / Deep (polymorphic Class=) / References (forward + cyclic) / Collections (list, set, dictionary)

Game root (Sim/Game.cs): owns World, the live Maps (a settlement's entered interior), and every manager that was previously only reached through Find (research, storyteller + CivilizationTarget, factions, letters, quests, scenario, family, social, god). Find.CurrentGame makes Find.* resolve through it when one exists and fall back to the pre-Game thread-static behaviour unchanged when it doesn't. Game.NewGame runs world generation, founds the starting settlement (SettlementFounder) and Scenario.PostGameStart against the actual founding population, then wires the defined pre/post tick order. Whole-game Scribe round trip (world + settlement + population + elapsed time), reloaded and re-ticked.
Autosave cadence and hook (Game.AutosaveIntervalTicks / Game.AutosaveDue): fires on a cadence wired into the post-tick order; writing the save file is left to the host, per the module's own scope

Streaming XmlWriter save path: ScribeSaver drives a System.Xml.XmlWriter rather than building an XDocument, which is what RimWorld's own saver always did. Scribe.SaveToStream/SaveToFile write straight to a sink, so content leaves as the writer's buffer fills and peak memory stops tracking save size; Scribe.SaveToXDocument/SaveToString keep their exact shape and text by pointing the same writer at an XDocument. Streaming adds one rule the port already obeyed — an attribute must precede its node's child content — and WriteAttribute now throws rather than silently dropping one. Loading still parses whole: the three-pass load re-reads nodes after cross-refs resolve, which a forward-only reader cannot serve

systems.translation: Unchanged per citizen. Adds aggregate 'public mood' rollups so the god view can read a city without opening every person.

items.label: Pawn skeleton + RaceProperties: needs/story/mind trackers, hash-interval ticking, Scribe round-trip
NeedDef set: Food, Rest, Joy, Mood, Beauty, Comfort, Outdoors, RoomSize (intelligence-gated)
Decay rules: food 1.6/day slowing when hungry, rest fall/gain with fatigue factors, joy tolerance, seekers
Thoughts: timed memories (stack limit, renew-oldest) + situational workers, trait nullifying/required
Mood = 50% + grouped thought total with RimWorld's geometric stacking rule; seeker rates
MentalBreaker bands (0.35/0.20/0.05), 2000-tick grace, MTB rolls, weighted trait-filtered break table, state lifecycle + Catharsis
TraitDef/Trait/TraitSet with degrees, conflicts and exclusion tags
Core XML: Human/Husky races, needs, joy kinds, traits, thoughts, mental states and breaks

Social/opinion thoughts and social fights: Thought_Memory carries a nullable otherPawn and feeds opinion (ThoughtDef.IsSocial, ThoughtStage.baseOpinionOffset) as well as mood; the Social module's interaction workers gain those memories, so chitchat/deep talk/insult/slight move opinion. A social fight is a real MentalStateDef (MentalState_SocialFighting) that trades blows through Combat's existing Verb_MeleeAttack/MeleeVerbUtility path rather than a parallel system, and ends at the Def's duration/MTB recovery or the instant either side goes down. Situational relation-driven thoughts (HasFriend/HasRival, via the generic ThoughtWorker_HasDirectRelation) stand in for RimWorld's spatial "friend nearby"/"rival present" thoughts, since no Map/room concept reaches this seam yet.

Translation: population mood rollups for the god view. Satisfied by God/GodRollup.cs's MeanMood — a population-weighted mean of Need_Mood.CurLevelPercentage, tier-aware (a Statistical citizen's need is cohort-sampled the same as any other, real or folded from a Settlement's bare StatisticalPopulation count), cached with a recompute cadence and an explicit dirty flag, fed by a real Settlement (or several, for a civilization) as of god.settlement-population. See docs/spec/simworld-spec.md §10's Aggregation bullet.

systems.translation: Unchanged.

items.label: BodyDef part tree: tags, groups, height/depth, coverage → absolute coverage for hit selection (Human + quadruped)
Hediffs: severity-staged conditions with comps (immunizable, tend duration, severity/day, disappears, gets-permanent, infecter); injuries, missing parts, added parts
11 capacities from part efficiency (tag averages, limb products, cap mods); downed = pain shock / unconscious / no legs, dead = lethal capacity, core part, lethal severity or 150 total damage
DamageDef → worker → injury on a coverage-weighted part; solid parts crack, skin bruises; part destruction removes the subtree
Pain aggregate (Σ offsets × Π factors) → consciousness penalty, pain shock, Pain/Sick thoughts
Bleeding → blood loss (lethal at 1), natural healing 8/day (+4 lying, +22×quality tended), scars, infection rolls, tending priority
Immunity vs severity race per disease (flu survivable, plague/infection lethal untended); malnutrition from starvation; hediff hunger/rest factors
Core XML: 23 part tags, 13 groups, 38 part defs, 2 bodies, 11 capacities, 16 hediffs, 6 damages, health thoughts

Drug ThingDefs (Beer/Alcohol, Flake/Yayo) carry a real CompDrug: tolerance builds per dose and decays per day (HediffCompProperties_SeverityPerDay, already existing), addiction rolls once tolerance is at ChemicalDef.minToleranceToAddict, and a further dose once addicted relieves severity instead of stacking a second addiction. Withdrawal reaches Need_Mood purely through content pointed at the pre-existing ThoughtWorker_Hediff hook (Thoughts_Drugs.xml) — no new Needs/Thoughts code. A dose's joy uses the existing Chemical JoyKindDef. Deliberately out of scope, and not RimWorld-sourced: overdose, and any chance of an addiction curing itself outright (see CompDrug's own remarks). Tests: tests/SimWorld.Core.Tests/Health/DrugTests.cs.

Surgery bills with skill-rolled outcomes: RecipeDef.isSurgery + a Class=-selected Recipe_Surgery worker (amputate, excise a hediff, install a part), queued as a Bill_Medical on the patient’s own bill stack. Success is the surgeon’s Medicine skill times the recipe’s difficulty; a failure injures the patient and may kill them, never silently nothing. Two surgeries ship as content; installing a prosthetic now ships as content too (InstallSimpleProstheticLeg) — see health.prosthetic-items

Prosthetics as real items: SimpleProstheticLeg ThingDef (Item, hasQuality + CompProperties_Quality, MarketValue set) ships tradeable — no crafting recipe, since no fabrication workbench exists yet (the same "craftable or tradeable" allowance this item took). InstallSimpleProstheticLeg ships as content, naming the item as a RecipeDef.ingredients entry; SurgeryUtility.PerformNextSurgery gained an optional ingredientsOnHand parameter so a bill naming ingredients only fires once a matching Thing is supplied and consumed (decremented/destroyed) — every ingredient-less surgery (amputate, excise) is unaffected, matching RecipeDef.ConfigErrors' existing surgery/non-surgery split. Tests: tests/SimWorld.Core.Tests/Health/SurgeryTests.cs.

systems.translation: Built: standing civilization-scale roles (RoleDef) replace a per-person priority grid. A role names the work types it emphasizes; Pawn_WorkSettings.ApplyRole sets those to the pawn's best priority (1) and leaves everything else at the default (3), rather than a player setting twelve numbers per citizen. Kept distinct from an EdictDef's own 'leaves no trace' guarantee (docs/spec/simworld-spec.md §10): a role is standing, not temporary, and does write into the priority grid — but Pawn_WorkSettings tracks every work type a caller set directly (SetPriority), and a role's own writes always skip those, so assigning or changing a role can never overwrite a person's own explicit choice; clearing a role (SetRole(null)) reverts every non-manual entry it touched back to default, the standing-policy mirror of an edict's guarantee. WorkPolicyUtility.ApplyRoleToPopulation is the civilization-scale lever — one call assigns a role across an entire settlement's citizens, the same 'act on the aggregate' shape GodManager gives edicts.

items.label: SkillDef/SkillRecord/Pawn_SkillTracker: levels 0–20, per-pawn records in listOrder, daily xpSinceMidnight reset
XP curve 1000→30000, passion 0.35/1/1.5, 4000 xp/day saturation, level up/down
Unused-skill decay: levels 10+ lose 0.1–8.0 XP per 200-tick interval; below 10 never decays
Work tags from traits disable skills and work types; backstory hook
Pawn_WorkSettings: priority grid per work type, 0–4, useWorkPriorities on/off collapse, disabled types forced to 0
WorkGiverDef ordering: emergency first, priority → naturalPriority → priorityInType; scanning wired to real WorkGiver_Scanner subclasses by the AI module (system 9)
Core XML: 12 SkillDefs, 20 WorkTypeDefs, 27 WorkGiverDefs, Pyromaniac disables Firefighting

Skill-driven stats: StatDef.skillNeedOffsets/skillNeedFactors (SkillNeed_Direct valuesPerLevel tables, SkillNeed_BaseBonus base+bonusPerLevel) resolved by StatWorker.GetValueUnfinalized off the pawn's own SkillRecord level, Class= polymorphic in content like this repo's other worker lists. Content: new WorkSpeedGlobal, MedicalTendQuality, MiningSpeed, ConstructionSpeed, CookSpeed and ResearchSpeed StatDefs, plus skillNeedOffsets added to the already-shipped ShootingAccuracyPawn/MeleeHitChance/MeleeDodgeChance. RimWorld's own curve numbers were not sourceable in this sandbox (see Stats_Work.xml's own remarks) — every curve here is this port's own invention, pinned by trend tests (higher skill gives a higher value, level 0 gives the plain base) rather than any literal.

Backstory-disabled work, landed end to end now that Pawn Generation exists (pawngen.backstory): BackstoryDef.workDisables/skillGains ship as content (Backstories_Civil/Tribal.xml, e.g. NobleChild/Scientist/TribalElder each disable real work), PawnGenerator assigns backstories and applies their skill gains, and Pawn.WorkTagIsDisabled/WorkTypeIsDisabled plus Pawn_WorkSettings consult them — a backstory-disabled work type is zeroed out of the priority grid and dropped from work-giver scanning exactly like a trait-disabled one, proven from this module's own side in WorkTests (pawngen.backstory's own tests prove it from pawn generation's side).

Translation: policy/role-driven priorities at civ scale — RoleDef.emphasizedWorkTypes; Pawn_WorkSettings.SetRole/ApplyRole write emphasized types to top priority and everything else to default, skipping any work type a caller set directly (manualPriorities) so a role never overwrites a person's own preference and un-assigning one leaves no trace; WorkPolicyUtility.ApplyRoleToPopulation applies a role across a whole population at once. Four roles ship as content (Farmer, Miner, Artisan, Scholar).

systems.translation: Implemented: think tree and jobs unchanged; the god issues edicts and goals that enter the tree above routine work instead of draft orders. Pathfinding is now shared for full-agent populations: AI.RegionPathCorridorCache builds one region-graph BFS tree per unique destination (paid once, reused by every pawn walking there, invalidated wholesale when RegionAndRoomUpdater.Version moves) and PathFinder tries a corridor constrained to it before falling back to its original unconstrained A* — a corridor can never be wrong (any doubt falls back to the always-correct search) but its region-hop-count metric is not cell distance, so a hierarchical route can be longer than optimal, disclosed and bounded by PathSharingTests rather than hidden. Measured (docs/perf/baseline.md §9): before/after speedup grows with population, from ~1.5-2.5x at N=100-1,000 to 9.7x at N=10,000 — an asymptotic (roughly O(N²) to O(N)) improvement for the 'N pawns to a shared destination' case, not just a constant factor.

items.label: ThinkTree priority nodes (ThinkNode_Priority, ThinkNode_Conditional guards, ThinkNode_JobGiver leaves) + a real Humanlike ThinkTreeDef: danger/mental-state > needs > directed orders > routine work > idle wander
Job + JobDriver toil state machine (Toil, ToilCompleteMode, Toils_General/Goto/Reserve, FailOn conditions) with Pawn_JobTracker driving it from Pawn.Tick
ReservationManager per map: claim/release/CanReserve, released automatically on job end, Scribe round-trip

Reachability answers via BFS over the Map/RegionGrid graph (mapcore.regions) instead of its own flat flood-fill cache: a passability change now dirties and rebuilds only the region(s) it touches, not the whole map, and a query walks a handful of coarse regions rather than every cell on the shortest path. CanReachTarget/CanReach's public shape is unchanged

A* (PathFinder) on the per-cell cost grid: array-backed binary min-heap open list, generation-stamped node info (no per-search clear), diagonal move with corner-cutting rules, pooled PawnPath, Pawn_PathFollower driving pawn movement at zero per-tick steady-state allocation

Hierarchical path sharing over the Region/RegionLink graph: AI.RegionPathCorridorCache builds a BFS corridor tree once per unique destination region-set and shares it across every pawn walking there; PathFinder tries the corridor first and always falls back to its original unconstrained A* on any doubt, so a corridor can narrow a search but never make it wrong. Correct but not always optimal (hop-count corridor can be geometrically longer than the true shortest path — bounded by test, not hidden). Measured: before/after speedup on 'N pawns to a shared destination' grows from ~1.5-2.5x at N=100-1,000 to 9.7x at N=10,000 (docs/perf/baseline.md §9) — flow fields not attempted; the region-graph corridor already delivers the asymptotic win this item needed

A real second ThinkTreeDef (Animal) selected by RaceProperties.intelligence — JobGiver_AnimalFlee plus the shared eat/sleep/wander givers, no work/edict/directed-order tiers. Taming as a roll (TameUtility.TryTame) scored off the tamer's Animals skill against RaceProperties.wildness; failure can anger the animal at its tamer (Pawn_MindState.angryAt/tameness), rerouting its tree via ThinkNode_ConditionalAngryAtHandler instead of the Combat-module attack RimWorld's manhunter would trigger. Training as TrainableDef/TrainabilityDef + Pawn_TrainingTracker: steps accumulate per session and decay if untended past a grace window. WorkGiverDefs TameAnimals/TrainAnimals (already-shipped placeholders) wired to real scanners + JobDriver_Tame/JobDriver_Train.

Translation: god edicts/goals as high-priority think nodes — built as JobGiver_Edicts, sitting between JobGiver_DirectedOrder and JobGiver_Work; see the god system's own entry for the full picture (EdictDef/EdictWorker, GodManager, the rollup)

The Warden work type wired to real scanners: WorkGiver_Warden_AttemptRecruit (WardenAttemptRecruit WorkGiverDef, JobDriver_Warden_AttemptRecruit + the PrisonerAttemptRecruit JobDef) drives the recruit/chat interaction combat.capture's Pawn_GuestTracker/WardenUtility already implemented but nothing called outside a test; WorkGiver_Warden_Feed (WardenFeed WorkGiverDef, JobDriver_Warden_Feed + FeedPatient) carries food to a downed, hungry prisoner and feeds it directly. WardenDeliverFood stays the WorkGiver_Pending placeholder — see that WorkGiverDef's own XML comment: this port has no room/prison-cell system, so a non-downed prisoner already reaches food entirely on its own via the ordinary JobGiver_GetFood tier, leaving RimWorld's ambulatory-prisoner DeliverFood case with nothing distinct to cover here. A downed hostile captured by CaptureUtility now ends up recruited (or its resistance worn down) purely through a colonist's own work-giver scan, not a utility called directly by a test.

HaulGeneral wired to a real scanner: WorkGiver_Haul finds a spawned Item-category Thing (this port's own ThingDef.EverHaulable, since no separate alwaysHaulable/held-vs-loose distinction exists — nothing here can hold an item the way an equipment/apparel tracker would) not already sitting in a Zone_Stockpile cell whose ThingFilter allows it, and JobDriver_HaulToCell (HaulToCell JobDef) carries it to the nearest reachable, reservable stockpile cell with room (HaulAIUtility.TryFindBestStockpileCell) — nearest to the item, not the pawn, matching RimWorld's own StoreUtility. A destination cell already holding the same def merges the stack (count exactly summed); an empty one gets a freshly made Thing carrying the same Stuff. No matching stockpile (or every one already full) is an honest 'no job', not an invented dumping ground — this port has one storage kind and no priority tiers, so that is StoreUtility's whole job here. Carrying itself is modelled the same abstract way JobDriver_HaulToBuildingSite and JobDriver_Warden_Feed already do (no carry-tracker exists): the source stack's count drops the moment the pawn reaches it, nothing visibly follows the pawn to the stockpile. HaulCorpses (same WorkGivers.xml file) stays WorkGiver_Pending — no Corpse class exists anywhere in this codebase, so it cannot be wired honestly.

JobGiver_GetRest claims a real bed before falling back to the ground: AI.RestUtility.FindBedFor is a trim of RimWorld's own RestUtility.FindBedFor (nearest reachable, unclaimed Building.ConstructionThingDefOf.Bed — no owned/medical/prisoner bed distinctions exist yet, so every bed is open to anyone), reserved like any other claimed target (Toils_Reserve.Reserve) so two pawns never converge on the same one. JobDriver_LayDown walks to whichever target it got — a bed or the pawn's own position — and sets Need_Rest.lastRestEffectiveness from Need_Rest.BedRestEffectiveness (unsourced constant, chosen only to sit above the ground's own documented 1 and pinned by a test that a bed rests a pawn faster than the ground, never trusted as the literal) once there. No ownership/assignment UI — RimWorld's own CompAssignableToPawn — was built; a bed is first-come, matching what this port's Bed content actually needs.

systems.translation: Translated: a chronicle-style narrator (name open — Scribe / Historian / The Chronicle) targeting the player's civilization. Threat points scale with civilization wealth, population and era instead of one colony.

items.label: Storyteller personas (Cassandra/Phoebe/Randy) built from comps: OnOffCycle, RandomMain, ClassicIntro, SingleMTB, Disease
Threat points: wealth and per-pawn curves × difficulty × adaptation × days-passed, clamped 35–10000
IncidentDef/category/target tags, workers (disease applies a hediff; threat/trade/wanderer placeholders), refire and gating rules, incident queue
Quiet-time adaptation factor rising with peaceful days, dropping on downs and deaths

Translation: narrator record (chronicle entries) and persona hook — name still open. Curated as history, not only a log: MomentCurator (owned deep-Scribed alongside the chronicle, like StoryWatcher_Adaptation/IncidentQueue) flags a chronicle entry a moment on first occurrence of its category (an incident's own defName, "Death:<cause>", or the text before a free-form line's first colon — no call-site changes needed), always for an era transition (spec §10: "reaching an era is an event, not just a readout"), and on a new longevity-at-death record; each rule is independently bounded in count so a routine century produces a handful of moments, never hundreds — see the quests system's own quests.moments item, which this mechanism belongs to.

Raid squad generator: IncidentWorker_RaidEnemy picks a hostile faction and a tech-gated RaidStrategyDef, spends points against that faction's own PawnGroupMaker/PawnGenOption roster (PawnGroupMakerUtility.ChoosePawnGenOptionsByPoints) so a neolithic faction structurally cannot field an industrial raider, and generates full, armed, faction-attributed pawns. Spawns them at a map edge when CivilizationTarget.Map is wired (no game wires one yet — nothing links a physical Map to the civilization-scale incident target); otherwise the squad is generated and handed back unspawned. The actual arrival-and-fight-the-player loop needs AI/Map and is not this item's scope.

Translation: era-based scaling — the current era multiplies threat points (standing in for the wealth term nothing computes yet), and IncidentDef.minEra/maxEra gate an incident to the ages it belongs to

Translation: the storyteller targets a civilization of several settlements. CivilizationTarget stops being told what the civilization is and derives it from the player faction's own Settlements — the roster is their citizens, the seat is the oldest one (ties broken by tile, so list order never decides), and PlayerWealthForStoryteller is the market value of what they hold, the wealth term EraDef.threatPointsFactor was written as a stand-in for. An incident that has to happen somewhere picks a settlement weighted by population, never below weight 1 so an emptied town cannot vanish from the story, and a raid arrives at that settlement's interior map when someone has entered it. One StoryState still covers the whole civilization: a raid this decade is a fact about the civilization, not about a town. Fixes in passing a roster that counted every citizen on the planet, rival civilizations included, once EmergenceManager started founding them

systems.translation: Unchanged mechanics; armies are groups of full agents.

items.label: Verbs: warmup → burst → cooldown state machine; ranged shot reports (accuracy^distance, weapon bands 3/12/25/40, target size, cover) and melee hit/dodge from skill curves
Armor: DamageArmorCategoryDef (Sharp/Blunt/Heat), ArmorUtility deflect/halve rolls, Sharp→Blunt diminish, penetration; wired into DamageWorker_AddInjury
Weapon and projectile content: knife, club, bow, revolver, assault rifle; tool capacities and maneuvers

Cover: CoverInfo/CoverUtility wired to real map geometry — Map.GenSight (Verse.GenSight-style Bresenham line of sight, decompiled-source-verified) gates a shot, CoverUtility.CalculateCoverGiverSet (the real 8-adjacent-cell, angle- and distance-weighted algorithm) resolves automatically from caster/target position once both are spawned on a map; a pawn behind a wall is measurably harder to hit than one in the open

Turrets (CompTurretGun: hostile-pawn scan throttled to a 15-tick hash interval, fires the existing Verb/ShotReport pipeline — caster widened from Pawn to Thing for this), traps (CompTrap: armed, springs once on the first non-owning-faction pawn to enter, then spent), explosions (Combat.GenExplosion: GenExplosion/DamageWorker_AddInjury-style radial cells-to-hit with line-of-sight wall blocking, optional linear damage falloff) — all plain ThingDefs with comps, the Building module's existing shape rather than RimWorld's own distinct Building_TurretGun/Building_Trap subclasses

Downed → captured → prisoner loop: CaptureUtility (downed + hostile-faction → Pawn_GuestTracker) and WardenUtility (resistance reduction → recruit, or release), GuestStatus/PrisonerInteractionModeDef kept as RimWorld's own names. Pawn_GuestTracker lives on the host Faction (Faction.prisoners), not on Pawn — Pawns/** is another lane's module and carries no such field; see Pawn_GuestTracker.cs's own remarks. The Warden WorkGiver/JobDriver that sends a colonist to actually carry this out is AI/Work content and code — see the ai system's own ai.warden entry.

systems.translation: Proposed: bills unchanged; guilds and industries act as bill queues at scale.

items.label: Bills and BillStack: repeat modes (count, target with hysteresis, forever), skill gating, suspend, ordering
Ingredient selection by value getter over candidate stacks, splitting and mixing rules — stockpile scanning lands with AI
Skill-driven quality generation with inspiration; trader and base-gen rolls
Cooking recipes, skill-driven food poisoning, eating and nutrition
ThingFilter over a ThingCategoryDef tree, with stuff categories, quality and hit-point ranges

Animal husbandry: RaceProperties.meatDef/leatherDef feed Recipe_ButcherAnimal (isButchery RecipeDef, applied straight to a dead animal pawn like a surgery — no Corpse thing exists, so ButcherUtility.TryButcher is the same no-job-driver call shape SurgeryUtility already established), yield scaled by body size (HusbandryTuning). CompMilkable/CompShearable/CompEggLayer (shared CompHasGatherableBodyResource base) fill toward 1 over a per-species interval and spawn real Milk/WoolAnimal/EggAnimalUnfertilized items on Gather. New content: Muffalo (milk+wool) and Chicken (eggs) beyond the already-shipped Husky, so wildness/produce variety is real.

Translation: guilds and industries as bill queues at civilization scale. A GuildDef names the RoleDef that staffs a guild, the skill its craftsmen are measured by and the recipes it may queue; a Guild holds a real BillStack — repeat modes and target-count hysteresis unchanged — but belongs to a Settlement, draws fixed ingredients from that settlement's Stores ledger and puts products back into it. Members are the settlement's citizens carrying the role, plus an assigned share of the Statistical cohort whose skill is one deterministic cohort sample, GodRollup's own idiom. Labour banks across intervals (WorkAccumulated) so a batch costing more than one interval can be finished at all, and a guild with no runnable bill banks nothing. Not modelled, all for the same reason — it belongs to the settlement interior: no workbench Thing, no hauling, no job driver. A recipe whose ingredients are a category filter is refused in ConfigErrors rather than silently skipped: a def-count ledger has no stockpile to choose between candidates in

systems.translation: Translated: a large authored tech tree detailing societal evolution across eras. Data model leaves room for procedural/endless tech later.

items.label: Research project DAG: prerequisites, hidden prerequisites, cycle detection
Research manager: progress, tech-level cost factor (+50% per level above), completion events, Scribe
IResearchUnlockable and ResearchProjectDef.UnlockedDefs: the mechanism that computes what a project unlocks from every def that names it

Content wired to it: ThingDef and RecipeDef implement IResearchUnlockable, and the buildings, weapons and recipes that exist are gated on projects that exist — a stove on Cooking, a stonecutter's table and sandstone blocks on Masonry, a bow on Bows, pemmican on FoodPreservation. A club stays ungated: a stick is not a technology.
Eras turn on their spine (the projects something else depends on) rather than on 100% of their content, so a dead-end flavour project cannot bar the next age
ResearcherTechLevel rises with the era instead of being set once at scenario start — it was silently taxing the whole tree 2.5x from a tribal start

Entering an era is an event: fired once per era crossed (derived from before/after the project finish, so loading a save never re-announces history), it writes a chronicle line and a letter, and a scenario’s starting era is seeded silently rather than narrated

Pacing, re-framed after the horizon decision: years are not the currency, so "can a 50-year civilization have everything" is a question about a unit that no longer applies. Measured per era instead — how much of an era a civilization has seen when it leaves it, and whether two archetypes see the same things. Answer: seen% lands within 2-4 points of the era’s spine share in every era, so cost tuning moves how MUCH gets done and never WHAT, and overlap never falls below ~0.85 at any price. Do not re-price the tree (docs/research/tech-reachability.md §10)

Divergence authored into the tree, not priced for: gen_techtree.py was restructured (68 prerequisite edges de-linearized, protecting the 22-node deep chain and every same-or-earlier-era/no-cycle invariant) and given 13 new leaf projects in previously all-spine track/era cells. Spine fraction fell from 48-85% (median ~72%) to 28-54% (median ~41%) per era, and the harness's eras command shows seen% and archetype overlap measurably lower in every era at the shipped throughput — see docs/research/tech-reachability.md §11
Translation: EraDef ladder (Sticks & Stones → Exotic) with per-era progress and current/next era
Core XML: research tab, 8 eras, a 30-project seed tree across the first eras
Authored tech tree of societal evolution: 245 projects across 8 eras and 14 tracks, generated from tools/content/gen_techtree.py

Translation: procedural tech past the authored tree. An EndlessResearchDef is content naming a tag of the authored tree to continue, title fragments to name refinements with, and a cost that grows; EndlessResearch mints a ResearchProjectDef per track per tier into the global DefDatabase, so every consumer — cost, gating, progress, the letter on completion — handles a generated project with exactly the code that handles an authored one. Derived rather than rolled: defName, label, cost and prerequisite are pure functions of track and tier, so a save stores one integer (the tier reached) and reloads byte-identical tech instead of a growing list of invented defs. Minted only when nothing in the authored tree can be started, so it costs a civilization that has not finished the tree nothing. Generated projects carry no era and so cannot hold the ladder open — the era ladder is a finite authored artefact that ends at Exotic, and this is what comes after it

The Research WorkTypeDef gets a real worker: WorkGiver_Research (a WorkGiver_Scanner, Research's own giverClass in WorkGivers.xml) scans for a reachable, unclaimed ResearchBench and issues JobDriver_Research, which walks to it and every tick adds ResearchManager.ResearchPointsPerWorkTick * pawn.GetStatValue(StatDefOf.ResearchSpeed) to CurrentProj through the real ResearchManager.ResearchPerformed — the ResearchSpeed StatDef's first real consumer, replacing the stand-in speed(skill) curve docs/research/tech-reachability.md had to model by hand. A bench is required, matching RimWorld: none built, or none reachable/unclaimed, and the giver simply finds no job; ResearchBench (Data/Core/Defs/ThingDefs_Buildings/Buildings_Research.xml) carries no researchPrerequisites of its own, so this can never be a lock a civilization cannot build its way out of, and it is buildable through the ordinary Blueprint/Frame/GenConstruct pipeline like any other building. ShouldSkip short-circuits the scan when CurrentProj is null; a project finishing mid-toil ends the job Succeeded the same tick rather than leaving the pawn idling with nothing current. Also grants Intellectual xp per tick (0.1, RimWorld's own JobDriver_Research value, named in tech-reachability.md's own assumption table)

systems.translation: Decided: other civilizations are the factions (unchanged); trade routes between settlements replace RimWorld's orbital/caravan traders as the connective tissue, priced the same way CoalSupply already prices coal (a real path through the world pather, marked up by distance) and closed while the two settlements' factions are at war; goodwill becomes diplomacy through two new layers RimWorld has no equivalent of — an explicit War/Peace state per relation (Faction.DeclareWar/MakePeace, entry and exit acts rather than goodwill silently crossing a threshold) kept separate from the existing Hostile/Neutral/Ally goodwill-derived label, and Def-driven Treaty terms (non-aggression, trade access) a pair of factions can sign, each with its own duration and goodwill effect. Every number here (war/peace goodwill swings, route premium, treaty terms) is this port's own judgement call, not sourced from RimWorld — see the code's own comments for where and why.

items.label: Faction relations: goodwill clamped to ±100, hostile/neutral/ally thresholds, permanent enemies, initial relations and natural drift
Market value as the trade unit with PriceType tiers
Buy and sell pricing with a negotiator Social-skill gain curve
Caravans: world path grid and finder over hilliness, biome and roads; ticks per move from the slowest pawn; food drain and arrival

CoalSupply: a settlement's access to coal, local deposit or the cheapest reachable settlement that has one via the caravan pathfinder, priced through the existing TradeUtility buy markup plus a route-distance premium — the predicate/cost a later era-transition or industrialisation check reads

FactionDef.pawnGroupMakers: PawnGroupKindDef/PawnGenOption/PawnGroupMaker plus FactionDef.GetGroupMaker — the squad-composition roster director.raids spends threat points against; each raiding FactionDef's own maker list is the tech gate (a neolithic faction's maker never lists an industrial PawnKindDef)
Traders: TraderKindDef with trade sessions and deals — stock generation and visiting traders land with Things/AI
Translation: civilization diplomacy — treaties, wars and trade routes between civilizations

systems.translation: Implemented: unchanged mechanics; settlements grow from citizen initiative plus god edicts rather than direct placement of every wall — SettlementConstructionInitiative decides what a settlement needs and places the blueprint, and an active edict (EdictDef.prioritizedConstruction) biases which unmet need gets filled first; see building.initiative.

items.label: Zone/Zone_Stockpile/Zone_Growing/ZoneManager (one zone per cell, Scribe round-trip with cells) plus a map-wide Area/AreaManager for the home area, kept distinct from Zone per RimWorld's own split; WorkGiver_GrowerSow (cell-scanning) sows an active growing zone's empty cells, WorkGiver_GrowerHarvest harvests any harvestable-now Plant map-wide — Zone_Stockpile's ThingFilter is now a real hauling destination too: HaulGeneral is wired (system 9: AI — see ai.hauling) to AI.WorkGiver_Haul/AI.JobDriver_HaulToCell, which read Zone.cells and Zone_Stockpile.filter directly rather than through any new member on this class

Blueprint → frame → building via real AI jobs/toils/reservations: GenConstruct placement validity, WorkGiver_ConstructDeliverResourcesTo{Blueprints,Frames} haul materials (ThingDefCountClass costList), WorkGiver_ConstructFinishFrame spends work scaled by Construction skill (read directly, not via StatDef.skillNeedFactors — see this system's report) and rolls success/fail; a failed Frame refunds half its delivered materials and respawns a Blueprint

RoofCollapseUtility: a roofed, edifice-free cell needs a Fillage.Full edifice (wall or unmined rock) within a straight-line radius; losing its last one collapses it, removing the roof and dealing Blunt damage (more for a thick natural roof) to whatever is under it. Event-driven off Map.EdificeGrid.DeRegister, not a per-tick scan; built on neither the region graph nor Room/RoomGroup — both answer a different question (reachability partitioning / thermal enclosure) than "how far is the nearest wall" — see this system's report for the full reasoning. DestroyMode.WillReplace (declared, previously unused) stops Frame.CompleteConstruction's Frame→Building swap from reading its own momentary despawn as support lost

CompPower/CompPowerTransmitter/CompPowerTrader/CompPowerPlant/CompPowerBattery; PowerNetManager builds/merges/splits PowerNets incrementally off cardinal adjacency as comps spawn/despawn (never a full-map rebuild); brownout is a real RimWorld whole-net simultaneous cutoff once batteries are exhausted, not the brief's described per-trader priority order (see this system's report)

Room/RoomGroup flood-filled from the edifice grid (a Door still splits a Room but RoomGroup re-merges rooms joined only by one); per-RoomGroup temperature equalises toward Map.outdoorTemperature at a rate from boundary Insulation and cell count, pushed by CompHeatPusherPowered; no biome/season modulation of outdoorTemperature exists (it is a flat settable field — no biome/season/climate system to drive it yet)

Building.Plant grows on the long tick at fertility (TerrainDef.fertility) × light × temperature — RimWorld's own three-factor product; light derived from GenDate's day/night clock (no per-map longitude exists yet, so every map shares one clock — see this system's report) and temperature from a recalled-not-verified RimWorld curve (0 below freezing/above 58°C, full rate in a 10-42°C band); harvest yields ThingDef.plant.harvestedThingDef scaled by Growth. Content ships two sowable crops (Plant_Potato, Plant_Rice) plus WildPlant upgraded to the same real Plant class

Translation: citizen-initiated construction under edicts — SettlementConstructionInitiative reads a settlement's real Citizens count (never StatisticalPopulation: a Statistical citizen has no individual Pawn to physically house, by the tiering system's own design — see the class's own remarks), what is already built or already planned on its InteriorMap, and what its Stores ledger holds, then derives a small, concrete need list (a Bed per citizen, a handful of Wall blueprints once there is anyone to shelter, a StorageHut once Stores holds enough to want one) and places blueprints for the shortfall through the existing GenConstruct/Blueprint/Frame pipeline — nothing decided to place a blueprint before this pass. Placement samples cells at random off the ambient RandomStream rather than scanning the map, validated entirely by GenConstruct.CanPlaceBlueprintAt (never overlapping or blocking what is already there), throttled to ConstructionInitiativeTuning.MaxBlueprintsPerTick per gated call so a settlement with a large shortfall grows over many ticks rather than flooding its map at once. Self-gated on GenTicks.TickRareInterval, the same 'rare bucket, not a per-tick scan' shape GodManager.GodTick/Storyteller.StorytellerTick/Settlement.GrowthTick already use; a settlement nobody has entered has no InteriorMap and this is a deliberate no-op there, never a triggered generation. The edict seam: EdictDef.prioritizedConstruction (new field, same declarative/read-live shape as prioritizedWork) reorders which unmet need a settlement fills first while an edict naming it is active — GreatWorksMandate ships it as real content ('quarry and building site before anything else') — with no activation-time side effect, so deactivating leaves no trace. New buildable content: Bed and StorageHut ThingDefs with Blueprint/Frame pairs alongside the existing Wall. Bed is now wired into Need_Rest/JobGiver_GetRest (AI.RestUtility.FindBedFor, AI.JobDriver_LayDown — see ai.rest): a citizen actually claims and sleeps in the bed this system builds for them, resting faster than the ground. SettlementConstructionInitiative.Tick() is wired into Sim/Game.cs's WireTickHooks as a normal PostTicker, the civilization-wide entry point a host loop calls once per tick (mirroring God.GodTick()); a settlement's own Full-tier citizens are what actually walk over and build what it queues, once Settlement.SyncCitizenSpawns (settlements.citizen-presence) puts them on its interior map in the first place.

systems.translation: Opinions and social interactions ported for this pass, RimWorld's compatibility-factor mechanic (a stable hash of the two pawns) included; ideoligions become the religions and ideologies of your civilization — memes/precepts feeding thoughts through the existing pipeline, rituals with a quality resolution, and precept-granted roles are built (social.ideology); per-citizen ideoligion membership (certainty, conversion, an outsider penalty) is not, and one Ideo stands in for a whole civilization's belief for now — see that item's own label. DLC systems (genes, psycasts, anomalies), still proposed, evaluated per era. RimWorld's Thought_Memory/Thought_MemorySocial split is folded into one Thought_Memory class with a nullable otherPawn and a ThoughtDef.IsSocial property, rather than a second thought class; RimWorld's spatial "a friend is nearby"/"a rival is present" situational thoughts read this port's stored relations instead (no Map/room concept reaches Social or Thoughts yet), via one generic, content-driven ThoughtWorker_HasDirectRelation.

items.label: Opinion score (Pawn_RelationsTracker.OpinionOf) from relation type (family relations derived from demography's own ids; friend/rival/lover/ex-spouse stored as DirectPawnRelation), social memories about that specific pawn, personality traits (TraitDegreeData.opinionOffset), and a stable per-pair compatibility factor

Periodic interaction rolls on a 2,500-tick population sweep, selected by weight per pair (chitchat, deep talk, insult, slight); a low-opinion, low-mood insult can escalate into a social fight via the existing MentalStateDef machinery — MentalState_SocialFighting runs on both participants, cross-linked via otherPawn, and actually trades blows through Combat's own Verb_MeleeAttack/MeleeVerbUtility path, ending at the Def's own duration/MTB recovery or the instant either side goes down

Courtship and its ending. Two more InteractionDefs rather than a sweep of their own: InteractionWorker_RomanceAttempt weighs zero for anyone married, related, too young, already together or not liked enough, and acceptance turns on opinion plus the pair's stable compatibility factor; InteractionWorker_Breakup is offered only to a couple whose social memories of each other have gone negative — measured on memories alone, because total opinion also carries the Lover relation's own +20 (a couple happy because they are a couple) and the compatibility factor (two people who click could never fall out). A marriage ends as a divorce: both spouse ids cleared and a mutual ExSpouse recorded, the shape widowhood already used, leaving the household standing because a household here is a lineage rather than a residence. Deliberately absent: infidelity (a married citizen never courts) and orientation (no pawn carries one, and a gate the data cannot support would be invented)

Built: MemeDef/PreceptDef (memes are broad themes with slots; precepts are the specific rules, faithfully split), an Ideo runtime object generated from an IdeoDef preset and Scribe round-tripped, precepts feeding mood through the existing thought pipeline (ThoughtWorker_UnderPrecept, built directly on the ThoughtWorker_UnderEdict precedent — one PreceptWorker class serves opposing judgments, the mood sign lives in content), rituals with a quality resolution (RitualUtility: participant count, officiant-role presence, participant mood — the shape is RimWorld's, the numbers are this port's own, pinned by trend tests since RimWorld's own quality table could not be sourced here), and precept-granted roles (IdeoRoleDef, capped by maxHolders — a second concept from Work.RoleDef, not an extension of it, partly because the two class names would silently collide in Def-type resolution). Content ships two contrasting ideoligions (TheHearthway, TheForgeCovenant) whose precepts read the same citizen state and reach opposite mood conclusions, plus a ritual and a role each, working end to end. NOT built: per-citizen ideoligion membership (RimWorld's certainty/conversion/outsider-penalty) — one Ideo stands in for a whole civilization's belief, every Humanlike citizen assumed a member, which is exactly the much-larger design this item originally deferred; event-tracked precepts (cannibalism, corpse treatment) — no consumption/corpse event stream exists to read, so every shipped precept instead reads state another module already tracks durably (a trait, worn apparel, a role). IdeoManager is a thread-static self-gate in Social/Ideology, not a Find.Ideo — Sim/** was out of this pass's file ownership; wiring a real Find.Ideo/Game.Ideo slot is the follow-up.
Genes, mechanitor bandwidth, psycasts, containment — evaluated per era

systems.translation: Built: scenarios become civilization starts (era, biome, rivals — quests.starts); quests become narrator-issued historical moments (quests.moments). A moment is the narrator noticing something worth remembering — a first, a record, a turning point — rather than a line per routine event; the Chronicle already recorded births, deaths, edicts and era transitions unconditionally, so the missing piece was deciding which of those matter more. Built as MomentCurator, owned by the Storyteller (src/SimWorld.Core/Director) since that is where the Chronicle itself lives — see that system's director.chronicle item for the mechanism and its own report for why the code sits there rather than under Quests.
systems.module: src/SimWorld.Core/Quests · Scenario · Letters (quests.moments' curator lives in src/SimWorld.Core/Director — see director.chronicle)

items.label: ScenarioDef and ScenPart: starting conditions, forced traits, starting research and things
QuestScriptDef node graphs over a Slate: sequence, set, branch, delay, letter, reward, end — compiled into quest parts with unique signals
Letters and LetterStack with accept/expire timers; the director's GiveQuest incident offers by points, weight and refire days
Translation: civilization starts — era, rival-civilization count and biome scenario parts

Translation: narrator-issued historical moments — MomentCurator (src/SimWorld.Core/Director/MomentCurator.cs, owned deep-Scribed by Storyteller) flags a chronicle entry as a moment on the first occurrence of its category, always for an era transition, and on a new record for longevity at death; a moment death also promotes the pawn via Pawn_TierTracker.Notify_ChronicleNamed. Each rule is independently bounded in count (by distinct categories, by the fixed era ladder, or by a monotonic ratchet), pinned by test that a routine simulated century produces far fewer than a hundred moments.

Game-start orchestrator to run Scenario.PostGameStart and the quest tick loop — Sim/Game.cs: Game.NewGame founds the settlement then runs PostGameStart against its citizens, and QuestManager.QuestManagerTick is wired into the post-tick order (it had never been driven by anything before)

systems.translation: SimWorld original — RimWorld has no equivalent to port. A colony of twelve never needs generations; a civilization does. Built on the ported age/life-stage clock rather than a compressed one. Citizen tiering (§11.3) is the same idea pushed further: a civilization needs most of its population cheap, not absent — RimWorld's world-pawn precedent (identity/ageing kept, needs/jobs/health frozen off-map) generalised from "on the map or not" to "significant or not". Migration (demography.migration) closes the module's last open seam: MigrationManager mirrors the birth formula's own shape (base × (0.5 + quality) × a situational factor) for arrivals, where quality is the same per-citizen mood/food signal births already read, plus an era factor — a more advanced settlement has more to offer. Arrivals generate one adult migrant per successful roll and found their household through the existing FamilyManager.FoundHousehold(founder, null, tick) hook (built for exactly this); a settlement's bare Statistical cohort grows by the same closed-form percentage idiom Settlement.GrowStatisticalCohort already uses for births-minus-deaths, never by materialising real Pawns for it. Departures remove a distressed family's living members together from a caller-owned population list — the same list-mutation contract FamilyManager.DemographyTick already uses — but Settlement itself exposes no public way to shrink StatisticalPopulation or remove a citizen (World/** is out of this lane's bounds to add one), so the Settlement-aware overload can only ever floor migration at zero, never make it negative; see MigrationManager's own doc for the stated limitation.
systems.module: src/SimWorld.Core/Pawns — Family · FamilyManager · Pawn_RelationsTracker · DemographyTuning · Pawn_TierTracker · MigrationManager · MigrationTuning

items.label: Family as the unit of lineage: founders, surname drawn from the shared name banks, members, generation depth, living vs total counts; Pawn_RelationsTracker carries familyId, spouseId, motherId, fatherId

Marriage founds a new household rather than merging into an existing one — the rule that keeps a civilization from collapsing into one dynasty (Epoch measured 90% in a single household; SimWorld's 120-year regression ends at 0.8% across 284 households)
Birth roll per couple per interval, gated by fertility window, minimum birth interval and food security; only the shape of Epoch's formula is reused, every constant is SimWorld's own
Death from age as a hidden pre-rolled budget (lifeExpectancy ± spread) with no public accessor — the player never sees how long a citizen has left
The budget moves with the civilization: completed MedicineHealth research read at birth lengthens it; starvation intervals spend it and being fed again does not refund it
Births, marriages and deaths recorded to the chronicle through the storyteller

Population level-of-detail: PawnTier (Full/Interval/Statistical) and Pawn_TierTracker dispatch ticking by which list a pawn sits on (Normal for Full, Long for Interval and Statistical alike, told apart only by what the coarse tick does there) rather than an if-skip inside Pawn.Tick(); promotion/demotion by significance (attention, role, chronicle mention, relation to someone promoted), never proximity or elapsed time; promotion catch-up brings age (exact, via AgeTickMothballed) and needs (real bulk decay at Interval, cohort sampling at Statistical) current in one step. Measured: Interval ~135 µs/pawn-day, Statistical ~25-36 µs/pawn-day, against Full's ~14,000-34,000 (box-load-dependent; see docs/perf/baseline.md and spec §11.3) — roughly 100-1,000x cheaper per citizen.

Migration and household founding by immigration: arrivals scale with a settlement’s own mood/food quality and its era, founding households through FamilyManager.FoundHousehold’s single-founder hook; departures remove a distressed family from a caller-owned roster, and a settlement’s Statistical cohort moves in both directions (Settlement.RemoveStatisticalPeople), so somewhere worth leaving is as expressible as somewhere worth going. A settlement’s live Citizens list has no departure path — removing a named citizen is the settlement’s own business, and the caller-owned-list overload is what that case is for

systems.translation: The opening of the game and what a settlement is once it has an interior. Region-then-site founding, deposits derived from terrain, era-weighted site scoring, a settlement that is an entity rather than a def plus a tile, and rival civilizations that emerge from play — World.EmergenceManager — rather than existing at time zero. Every settlement anywhere, including world generation's own, is now a real Settlement founded through SettlementFounder; World.Settlements is typed Settlement, not a WorldObject mix. Closing the last gap in §11.2/§11.3's seam: Settlement.SyncCitizenSpawns places every Full-tier citizen (never Interval, never — by the tiering system's own design — a Statistical one) onto the interior map the instant it is entered, near whatever the settlement has already built, and reconciles that presence on a rare gated cadence after — dropping a citizen who died (off the map and off the roster, so population never keeps counting them) and moving one who leaves Full off the map without anyone tearing the interior itself down, since nothing in this codebase ever discards a generated map once cached. A citizen currently spawned is saved by reference to the one real copy the map's own Thing list already owns, never deep-saved a second time, so a round-tripped save neither duplicates nor loses anyone.
systems.module: src/SimWorld.Core/World (regions, deposits, siting, solo start, Settlement entity, SettlementFounder, EmergenceManager)

items.label: Region partition over the icosphere: contiguous tile groups cut on coastline, ridges and major rivers, each with a name, dominant biome, climate and summarised resource profile

Resource and landmark deposits derived from existing terrain — clay in floodplains, flint in chalk lowland, ore in hills, coal in ancient swamp/floodplain low ground, salt at coasts and springs, deep soil in valleys, timber by biome, fords and defensible high ground from elevation

Site score: hard necessities (fresh water, land that feeds the band, survivable climate) times era-weighted advantages (defensibility, transport, materials, trade position); advisory for the player, decisive for emergent foundings
Trade position scored by inverting the road pather — how many cheap routes would pass through a tile
Founding band of 20-40 in several households, all Full-tier, with a founding chronicle entry — SettlementFounder, built on FamilyManager.FoundHousehold

Settlement as an entity: population by tier (real Pawns for Full/Interval, a bare count for Statistical), stores as a def-count ledger, founding tick, name and growth wired to FamilyManager.DemographyTick (plus a closed-form top-up for the Statistical count, which that mechanism cannot run against — see the module's report). "Works" (production/workplaces) is not built — out of scope for this pass, tracked separately
Solo-start world generation: the player's faction alone at time zero

Settlement interior map generated on entry at settlement scope and persisted after — Settlement.EnterMap, sized by TotalPopulation via a named tuning ladder rather than a flat constant, generated once and cached, Scribe round-tripped (present only for a settlement actually entered)

Rival civilizations emerging from the simulation over time rather than being placed at world gen — World.EmergenceManager, ticked from World.WorldTick: a new civilization emerges with a real, live founding band via SettlementFounder.Found (chronicled), and an established civilization grows into a second settlement via the new SettlementFounder.FoundColony (a Statistical-population colony, no live band — routine growth, not an origin story). Every settlement world generation itself places is now a real Settlement too (SettlementFounder.FoundColony, unchronicled backstory), closing World.Settlements' old WorldObject/Settlement mix. Pacing (MTB years between events) is SimWorld's own, pinned by a simulated-span band test, not a literal; determinism (same seed, same emergence history) is tested via the manager's own persisted RandomStream

Coal as its own terrain-derived deposit (swampiness/rainfall/floodplain low ground, measurably distinct from Ore's hills and mountains), worth ~0 in site scoring before Medieval and the single highest advantage weight by Industrial, and tradeable via Economy.CoalSupply — a settlement without local coal can buy it from the nearest settlement that has it, at a real markup over sitting on your own deposit. CoalSupply now also reads a real Settlement's actual stores (additively, alongside the terrain signal — see the Settlement-entity module's report) rather than inferring access purely structurally

A settlement's Full-tier citizens are actually placed on its interior map, closing the gap every other module worked around: Settlement.EnterMap spawns every not-yet-spawned Full citizen (Settlement.SyncCitizenSpawns), placed by GenRadial nearest-first search out from the centroid of whatever the settlement has already built (the map's own centre before anything has), never a corner. Interval never spawns — no jobs, no mind state, spec §11.3's own words — and a Statistical citizen was never eligible to begin with (no live Pawn exists for one). Re-checked on SettlementTuning.CitizenMapSyncIntervalTicks (the same rare-tick bucket SettlementConstructionInitiative already uses): a citizen who died is dropped from Citizens and taken off the map (no Corpse system yet — Health's territory, not this one); a citizen who falls out of Full (a future attention system's demotion) is taken back off the same way, and one promoted back to Full is placed again — the real, reachable form of "release" this design has, since nothing anywhere discards an already-generated InteriorMap. Scribe-safe by construction: a spawned citizen is written as a reference to the one real Pawn the map's own deep Thing list already owns, an unspawned one deep-saved here as before, so a round trip neither duplicates nor loses anyone.

systems.translation: Unchanged.

items.label: StatRequest (Thing, or def+stuff with no Thing) -> StatWorker.GetValue: base value (statBases, else defaultBaseValue) -> skill-need factors, then skill-need offsets (system: work.stats) -> trait and hediff-stage offsets -> trait, hediff-stage and stuff factors -> capacity factors -> stat parts -> post-process curve -> min/max clamp

StatDef.capacityFactors reads the Health module's PawnCapacityDef levels (RestRateMultiplier: BloodPumping/Metabolism/Breathing at weight 0.3 each) so a wounded pawn's stats degrade and recover with the body

Pawn.RestRateMultiplier/ImmunityGainSpeed/PainShockThreshold/GlobalLearningFactor/MentalBreakThreshold and Armor.NaturalArmor.ArmorRating now read the pipeline instead of a hard-coded constant or a bare statBases lookup; the two duplicate StatDefOf classes (Crafting, Economy) are retired into one SimWorld.Stats.StatDefOf

Core XML: RestRateMultiplier, ImmunityGainSpeed, PainShockThreshold, GlobalLearningFactor, MentalBreakThreshold StatDefs (every default sourced from RimWorld's own vanilla values), BasicsPawn/Basics StatCategoryDefs, Human's MentalBreakThreshold moved from a RaceProperties field to a statBases entry

Closed properly, not by assertion: CompQuality (Things) gives QualityCategory a home on a live Thing; StatPart_Quality (Stats) is the first concrete StatPart this module ships, wired onto MarketValue's own content (Stats_Economy.xml); Thing.Stuff — plus ThingMaker applying it and StatRequest.For(Thing) reading it — finally gives the stuff factor/offset pass (real and tested since stats.pipeline, previously always fed StuffDef=null for a live Thing) something to read. Tests: tests/SimWorld.Core.Tests/Things/QualityAndStuffTests.cs (filed with CompQuality rather than under Stats, per this pass's test-directory ownership).

systems.translation: SimWorld's own — RimWorld has no equivalent to port. The re-focus from §10: the player is not a colony overseer but a god directing one civilization, so the player's own verb changes from drafting individuals to issuing standing civilization-scale edicts and reading aggregate rollups. Kept in RimWorld's own declarative shapes throughout even though the concept is new: Def + Worker + Class= polymorphism for EdictDef/EdictWorker (mirroring WorkGiverDef/WorkGiver and ThoughtDef/ThoughtWorker), IExposable for GodManager, a Find service exactly like Find.Storyteller/Find.ResearchManager, and a think-tree job-giver node for the work push rather than a bespoke priority mechanism. The mood consequence reuses the existing situational-thought pipeline (ThoughtWorker_UnderEdict) instead of inventing a second one, so an edict's cost to public mood appears and disappears with activation on its own, the same way every other situational thought already does.
systems.module: src/SimWorld.Core/God · EdictDef · EdictWorker · EdictWorker_ExemptMinors · ThoughtWorker_UnderEdict · GodManager · GodRollup · GodTuning; src/SimWorld.Core/AI/JobGiver_Edicts.cs · WorkGiverScanUtility.cs (shared with JobGiver_Work)

items.label: EdictDef: label/description (inherited from Def), prioritizedWork (List<WorkTypeDef>), an optional requiredEra (EraDef) gate read against ResearchManager.CurrentEra, an optional researchFocus (ResearchProjectDef) set as the current project on activation, a Class=-selected workerClass (EdictWorker) defaulting to the declarative base class, and a moodThought (ThoughtDef) granting a situational mood cost to every citizen the edict's AppliesTo(Pawn) reaches. EdictWorker_ExemptMinors ships as the one concrete worker exercising the Class= seam for something a def field alone cannot express (a harsh edict that spares children). Also carries prioritizedConstruction (List<ThingDef>, building.initiative): the same declarative, read-live shape as prioritizedWork, biasing which unmet need SettlementConstructionInitiative fills first rather than a second mechanism; GreatWorksMandate ships it as real content.

GodManager (Find.God): active edicts under a slot budget (GodTuning.MaxActiveEdicts, SimWorld's own number, pinned by test rather than trusted as a literal), CanActivate/Activate/Deactivate/IsActive/ActiveEdicts, a Chronicle line on activation and deactivation via Find.Storyteller.RecordChronicle, a self-gated GodTick on the long tick bucket (2000 ticks, GenTicks.TickLongInterval) matching Storyteller.StorytellerTick/FamilyManager.DemographyTick's own idiom, and a full Scribe round trip.

JobGiver_Edicts inserted into ThinkTrees_Humanlike.xml strictly between JobGiver_DirectedOrder and JobGiver_Work — a queued directed order and every need/mental-state guard above it still outrank a standing edict, and an edict only ever wins a job routine work would otherwise have offered, never pre-empting a need. Scans only the WorkGiverDefs under the active edicts' prioritizedWork types, sharing JobGiver_Work's own nearest-candidate scan via the new WorkGiverScanUtility rather than duplicating it. Never touches Pawn_WorkSettings: deactivating an edict leaves a citizen's own work priorities byte-for-byte unchanged, proved by test.

GodRollup: population (total and by PawnTier), mean mood, mean health, a food/industry readout (mean Need_Food level; mean Construction/Mining/Crafting skill as the industry proxy in the absence of a real production ledger), current era and its research progress. Tier-aware by construction: a Statistical citizen's health contribution is Pawn_TierTracker.SampledHealthFraction, never Pawn_HealthTracker's real hediff-driven summary — proved by test (a severely injured Statistical citizen's real health, ~0.27, never leaks into the rollup, which instead reports the cohort-sampled band). Cached with an explicit dirty flag (Notify_Dirty) and a recompute cadence, not recomputed per tick per reader.

EdictDefs/Edicts.xml: five edicts spread across the era ladder (HuntersMandate, BreakTheSod, GreatWorksMandate, IronDiscipline, IndustrialMobilization), each with a real requiredEra, prioritizedWork and researchFocus, and its own mood-cost ThoughtDef (ThoughtDefs/Thoughts_Edicts.xml, workerClass ThoughtWorker_UnderEdict). Zero config errors, zero DefOf errors.

GodRollup.Recompute(Settlement) and Recompute(IReadOnlyList<Settlement>) read a real Settlement's population by tier: Citizens (real Pawn objects, Full/Interval) walked exactly like the bare-list overload, StatisticalPopulation (a bare count with no Pawn per person) folded in by AccumulateStatisticalCohort — one deterministic RandomStream.RangeSeeded sample per settlement per statistic (mood, food, health, industry skill), seeded from the settlement's own identity and the current tick, reusing Pawn_TierTracker's cohort-sampling idiom rather than a second one, weighted by count in the running mean rather than walked member by member. Counts (TotalPopulation, StatisticalCount) include the cohort exactly; each mean's own doc comment states the weighted-sample choice. New GodTuning.StatisticalIndustrySkillSampleMin/Max (SimWorld's own, not RimWorld-sourced) stand in for the missing per-person SkillRecord. Proved by test: identical output to the bare-list overload when a settlement has no Statistical slice, correct weighting when it dominates, and a 100,000,000-person Statistical settlement recomputing in well under the per-citizen-loop budget (no enumeration proportional to StatisticalPopulation).

God/View: the engine-free contract the host binds to. GodViewSnapshot.Capture() takes one tick's values — civilization rollup, settlements, every edict with an EdictAvailability and a reason in words, chronicle tail and curated moments — and GodCommands issues or rescinds by defName, explaining every refusal in the same wording the snapshot used. Everything crosses the seam as strings and values: the host never holds a Def (so it cannot reach a worker) or a manager (so it cannot mutate state off-tick), and a test asserts that structurally. EdictOption.Availability == Available is pinned to agree with GodManager.CanActivate for every edict at both ends of the era ladder, so the view can never offer something the simulation would then refuse.

The god view itself — a presentation surface reading the read model below and offering edicts. Needs the Unity host: a headless container has no display, so nothing visual can be built or verified here. The contract it binds to is done (god.read-model); what is left is the surface.

GodManager subscribes to ResearchManager.EraReached (constructor for a fresh civilization, ExposeData's PostLoadInit branch for a loaded one, both through the idempotent EnsureSubscribedToEraTransitions so a loaded save can never end up doubly subscribed — proved by test) and reacts on every crossing: EdictDef gained obsoleteEra, the mirror of requiredEra (same minEra/maxEra symmetry as IncidentDef in Director/IncidentDefs.cs, but >= rather than >, since reaching the named era is itself the retirement moment per the brief) — an active edict past its obsoleteEra auto-deactivates with its own "Edict outgrown" Chronicle line. Separately, one "New edicts available" Chronicle line names every edict the crossing newly unlocks (never one per edict, never written when nothing unlocked). HuntersMandate ships with obsoleteEra=Agrarian as real content proving the mechanism, not just an ad-hoc test def.
